doc: Scans D_80085458[0..D_80073734[0]) for active slots (f1a != 0, f06 >= 0x10) whose key fields (f0a, f5c, f04) match the caller-supplied device/channel id encoded in arg0 (channel/device hi-byte in bits 8+, note/index in bits 0-6) and arg1 (device hi-byte in bits 8+). For each match: clears f1a/f0a, OR-accumulates D_80073740[i] into a running flags word, and re-dispatches the note twice via func_80056D44(i,&entry) each followed by func_8005E97C(0, D_80073740[i]). Sets D_80085F98[0]=1 for the duration, calls func_8005E97C(0, acc) at the end, then clears D_80085F98[0]. Likely a "stop matching active notes" (all-notes-off style) handler in the sound driver.

globals.decl: extern S_8005BAB0_85458 D_80085458[64]; /* stride 0x78 struct array; this function newly establishes fields f0a (u16 @0x0A) and f5c (u16 @0x5C) not touched by other reconciled siblings (w_80056A08.c/w_800564A8.c/w_80056408.c/w_80056948.c); f04 and f1a here must be typed u16 (not s16 as w_80056A08.c's write-only view has them) because this function READS them and the target uses lhu (zero-extend), not lh -- reconcile as u16 across any function that READS these two fields.

globals.decl: extern s32 D_80085F98[4]; /* forced hi/lo access via size > 8; mode/busy flag set to 1 for the duration of this function, cleared to 0 at the end (same idiom as w_8005863C.c/w_800585A0.c/w_8005AE90.c) */
